PullRequest.Title: chat: make cloud sandbox wake retries deadline-driven

## Summary

Keep initial cloud sandbox connections alive through transient request failures and pending wake responses, within the existing ten-minute connection deadline.

Previously, a single ten-second request timeout ended the entire connection attempt. Pending responses also exhausted a twenty-request limit well before the overall deadline.

- Give connect/reconnect requests a 30-second timeout without changing environment-read, discovery, or task-operation budgets.
- Distinguish unanswered network requests from explicit HTTP failures and retry the former after 30 seconds.
- Replace the twenty-response cutoff with the existing connection deadline.
- Follow pending `Retry-After` responses with a one-second minimum and positive jitter; cancel oversized waits at the deadline instead of retrying early.
- Preserve cancellation, terminal HTTP/authentication/setup errors, and the separate credential-completion retry limits.

Regression coverage includes recovery after more than twenty pending responses, readiness at 590 seconds, termination at 600 seconds, cancellation during retry waits, and zero/oversized server delays.

## Manual verification still needed

Connect to a sleeping cloud sandbox and verify that pending responses or a transient network interruption do not require another click, that a successful wake establishes the session, and that an environment which never becomes ready stops at the connection deadline. Verify cancellation stops further requests.

This changes VS Code's client retry policy only; it does not change server wake behavior or the AHP contract. Explicit HTTP failures, including 429, remain terminal for the initial connection.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The loop, delay, global deadline, network boundary, and caller coalescing are directly traced. The added test proves the long-wake cadence; only exact production response latency and rate-limit thresholds are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: authenticated HTTPS `/connect` calls plus per-call authentication lookup, telemetry, and logging
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Sequential requests grow with wake duration divided by Retry-After. At the tested one-second cadence, a 590-second wake produces roughly 500-plus calls. Normal callers coalesce to one loop per environment, so concurrency is one but cardinality is hundreds.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive I/O and reduced throughput under control-plane rate limiting
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The connection imposed a 5,000 ms minimum and stopped after 20 waking responses, so this scenario made at most 20 `/connect` calls.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A coalesced connection attempt now issues `/connect` requests for the full ten-minute deadline and honors a one-second Retry-After, rather than stopping after 20 attempts with a five-second floor.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 495 replaces the 20-attempt loop with an unbounded loop; the same diff lowers the pending-response client floor from 5,000 ms to 1,000 ms. The added 590-second test explicitly asserts more than 20 sequential requests at roughly one-second intervals.
Findings.Title: Bound deadline-driven wake polling
Findings.Impact: A sandbox returning `202 waking` with `Retry-After: 1` can cause roughly 500 authenticated HTTPS requests during one connect, increasing network/power use and consuming control-plane quota enough to risk rate-limiting this connection or neighboring Mission Control operations.
Findings.Evidence: Each `_mintWithWaking` iteration calls `CloudSandboxApiService.connect`, which resolves the auth session and invokes `_requestService.request` against the GitHub Copilot API. The loop is now attempt-unbounded, the floor is 1,000 ms, and cancellation occurs after 600,000 ms. The new 590-second test proves more than 20 calls at this cadence. This API service separately documents that a few dozen Mission Control requests can trip GitHub rate limits and starve later calls.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the overall deadline, but bound polling frequency by retaining the five-second client floor or backing off after the first few one-second polls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or explicitly connect to a sleeping cloud sandbox that repeatedly returns `202 waking`.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every pending `/connect` response and retry delay is on the user-visible session-open critical path until credentials are returned, followed by the pre-existing Web PubSub connection and handshake.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticated HTTPS GET to the GitHub Copilot Mission Control `/agents/environments/{id}/connect` endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously at most 20 calls with a five-second floor; now roughly wake-duration/Retry-After, about 500-plus calls in the added 590-second, one-second-response test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same path stopped after 20 pending responses and used at least a five-second delay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each response and delay gates credential readiness and therefore session activation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Establish the remote Web PubSub transport and agent-host protocol handshake.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One establishment attempt on this path, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The Web PubSub dial and protocol handshake must finish before connect returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One sandbox's wake duration and returned Retry-After; effective cardinality is hundreds for a near-deadline wake, after per-address coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Requests are sequential within one attempt. Normal cloud-session callers coalesce to one pending attempt per environment; different environments can still connect independently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no response cache for connection credentials, appropriately; each poll resolves the current authentication session and sends a fresh request. The session contribution coalesces in-flight connects by sandbox address, and a live remote connection is reused.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: loop cardinality, one-second floor, global deadline, request boundary, and caller coalescing are all directly visible and test-covered.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact production wake durations and endpoint quota thresholds are unknown, lowering severity, but the added test establishes that 590-second one-second polling is an intended supported case.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium network boundary fan-out: deadline-driven recovery is useful, but lowering the floor while removing the request cap amplifies one connect from at most 20 requests to hundreds.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial cloud-sandbox connect encounters unanswered network requests.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The failed request timeout and fixed retry delay are on the connection critical path; the outer ten-minute token cancels requests and waits.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retry unanswered authenticated `/connect` requests after a 30-second delay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most about ten sequential calls for full 30-second timeouts; immediate network failures can retry every 30 seconds, at most about twenty. Previously one request failed after its ten-second timeout with no retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A single unanswered request terminated the connection attempt after the shared ten-second request timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Retries delay terminal failure but can recover the same user action without another click; all work remains within the established ten-minute connection budget.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Elapsed connection deadline and network failure duration, not collection size; effective count is bounded to roughly 10-20.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One request at a time per coalesced environment attempt. A full 30-second request failure followed by a 30-second delay yields at most ten attempts within ten minutes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No negative cache is used for transient network failures. The same attempt is retried because the failure is classified as unanswered; successful live connections are still reused. Authentication sessions are looked up for each retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: error classification, timeout, delay, sequential await, and cancellation tests are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual network failures may complete before the 30-second request budget, but retry frequency is still bounded by the fixed 30-second delay and global cancellation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the retry boundary is intentional, sequential, coalesced, globally bounded, and paced at 30 seconds.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial token lacks a sealed GitHub credential and requires reconnect refreshes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A reconnect request for a missing sealed token is on initial authentication readiness, but the loop can fall back to the initial token after its bounded attempts. The outer connection deadline also applies.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 12 reconnect requests after the initial connect, unchanged; each request may now wait up to 30 seconds instead of 10 seconds, while the ten-minute outer deadline remains authoritative.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same maximum of 12 sequential reconnects with a five-second retry floor, but a ten-second per-request timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each reconnect wait delays establishment while seeking complete credentials.

Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sequential reconnect calls; no parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Credential responses are not cached beyond the staged current connection. The existing sealed-token retry loop remains capped at 12 attempts, and the changed helper call explicitly retains the prior five-second minimum.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the fixed attempt cap and preserved delay are directly test-covered.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Server reconnect latency distribution is unknown; extending the request budget may improve successful completion and does not increase request cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: request count remains bounded and sequential; the longer per-request timeout is within the existing overall deadline.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cloud sandbox connect succeeds immediately or receives an explicit HTTP/authentication/setup error.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The single connect request and subsequent unchanged handshake are on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initial `/connect` returning credentials or an explicit HTTP error.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One authenticated HTTPS connect request, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One request; only its timeout ceiling changed from 10 to 30 seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Its response determines whether the connection proceeds to handshake or fails.

Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One request for immediate success or explicit HTTP failure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No retry cache is relevant. Explicit HTTP responses remain terminal and successful credentials are staged for connection reuse.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: explicit HTTP errors are excluded from retries by type and covered across status codes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The distribution of server response times is unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: no added boundary cardinality, eager work, retention, or concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and traced connection, retry, cancellation, authentication, and handshake paths. Submitted one medium boundary-fan-out finding for the unbounded one-second pending-response polling loop; other retry paths are sequential, coalesced, and deadline/attempt bounded.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
